component.name: reveal-sdk-ai
component.description: Reveal SDK AI plugin for Java — adds AI capabilities to Reveal BI dashboards

properties.name: infragistics:scope
properties.value: AI wrapper plus the reveal-sdk-servlet 2.3.0 Maven runtime graph declared by its POM. The OS-selected reveal-sdk-engine 2.3.0 dependency is not inventoried here.

properties.name: io.revealbi.sbom.platform-resolution
properties.value: Platform independent. reveal-sdk-core 2.3.0 selects reveal-sdk-engine-<os>-<arch> 2.3.0 through OS-activated Maven profiles; that host-selected engine dependency was excluded during resolution and is not part of this inventory.

properties.name: io.revealbi.sbom.inventory-scope
properties.value: Published Maven compile/runtime dependencies of io.revealbi:reveal-sdk-ai:1.3.2 resolved from its released POM (Maven 3.9.16): reveal-sdk-servlet 2.3.0, reveal-sdk-core 2.3.0, Jetty 12.0.12, org.json, SLF4J API and Jackson 2.17.2, plus the .NET assemblies bundled under native/ in the JAR, identified as NuGet packages. When an application uses a newer Reveal Java SDK, the Reveal SDK, Jetty and related entries follow that SDK's dependencies, but jackson-databind still resolves to 2.17.2 because reveal-sdk-ai declares it directly, unless the application declares jackson-databind itself. Excluded: the OS-selected reveal-sdk-engine 2.3.0 JAR, host-provided assemblies the plugin loads from the Reveal engine, the provided servlet API, and host operating-system libraries.

properties.name: reveal:vex:assessment-scope
properties.value: Reveal AI 1.3.2 for Java (io.revealbi:reveal-sdk-ai) and Node (reveal-sdk-node-ai): the AI package, the bundled .NET assemblies, the Maven runtime dependencies of reveal-sdk-servlet 2.3.0 and the npm production dependencies of reveal-sdk-node 2.3.2. Not included: the OS-specific Reveal engine, host-provided .NET assemblies, the headless browser downloaded at runtime, and host operating-system libraries.

properties.name: reveal:vex:assessment-method
properties.value: Resolved the published POM and npm dependency graphs and identified the bundled .NET assemblies by assembly name, version and SHA-256 comparison with published NuGet packages. OSV-Scanner matched the inventoried packages against complete offline NuGet, npm and Maven databases. Each decision is based on the advisory prerequisites and a static review of the released packages; findings that depend on deployment configuration remain in_triage.

components.name: json
components.description: JSON is a light-weight, language independent, data interchange format. See http://www.JSON.org/ The files in this package implement JSON encoders/decoders in Java. It also includes the capability to convert between JSON and XML, HTTP headers, Cookies, and CDL. This is a reference implementation. There are a large number of JSON packages in Java. Perhaps someday the Java community will standardize on one. Until then, choose carefully.

components.name: System.Text.Json
components.description:
Provides high-performance and low-allocating types that serialize objects to JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) text and deserialize JSON text to objects, with UTF-8 support built-in. Also provides types to read and write JSON text encoded as UTF-8, and to create an in-memory document object model (DOM), that is read-only, for random access of the JSON elements within a structured view of the data.

The System.Text.Json library is built-in as part of the shared framework in .NET Runtime. The package can be installed when you need to use it in other target frameworks.

vulnerabilities.description: Jetty has HTTP Request Smuggling via Chunked Extension Quoted-String Parsing

analysis.detail: Request smuggling requires a front-end proxy that parses requests differently from Jetty. Reveal uses Jetty only for an internal HTTP/1.1 listener that the local Reveal engine connects to directly, and Reveal does not place a proxy in front of it. Reassess if a reverse proxy is deployed in front of that listener.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-databind: @JsonIgnore on a Record property is bypassed with a PropertyNamingStrategy

analysis.detail: Requires deserializing JSON into a Java record that uses @JsonIgnore while a property naming strategy is configured. Reveal deserializes JSON only into untyped JSON trees and maps, not into records or other bean types, and does not configure a naming strategy. Application code that uses Jackson directly is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-databind: @JsonView bypassed for @JsonUnwrapped container properties on deserialization

analysis.detail: Requires a bean property annotated with @JsonView and @JsonUnwrapped, deserialized with an active view. Reveal deserializes JSON only into untyped JSON trees and maps and does not use Jackson views. Application code that uses Jackson directly is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-databind has case-insensitive deserialization bypasses per-property @JsonIgnoreProperties

analysis.detail: Requires case-insensitive property matching together with @JsonIgnoreProperties on a bean type. Reveal deserializes JSON only into untyped JSON trees and maps and uses default ObjectMapper settings. Application code that uses Jackson directly is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-core: Number Length Constraint Bypass in Async Parser Leads to Potential DoS Condition

analysis.detail: Affects only Jackson's non-blocking (async) parser. Reveal parses JSON only with Jackson's standard blocking parser and does not use the non-blocking parser. Application code that uses Jackson directly is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-core: UTF8DataInputJsonParser._reportInvalidToken() missing maxErrorTokenLength limit -> unbounded StringBuilder growth (DoS)

analysis.detail: Affects only the parser Jackson uses for java.io.DataInput sources. Reveal does not parse JSON from DataInput sources. Application code that uses Jackson directly is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: Eclipse Jetty: HTTP Authority/Host mismatch

analysis.detail: The missing host check affects only Jetty's HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 support. Reveal configures Jetty for HTTP/1.1 only, and no Jetty HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 module is in the dependency graph.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-databind quadratic forward-reference completion

analysis.detail: Applies only to object identity handling (@JsonIdentityInfo) on bean types. Reveal deserializes JSON only into untyped JSON trees and maps, which do not use object identities. Application code that uses Jackson directly is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: Eclipse Jetty: Cross-Request Leakage for trailers on HTTP/1.1 keep-alive connections

analysis.detail: Affects only code that reads HTTP request trailers. Reveal does not read request trailers.

vulnerabilities.description: JSON-java: JSONTokener Has Unbounded Numeric String Resource-Exhaustion DoS

analysis.detail: reveal-sdk-core 2.3.0 declares org.json 20231013, but no Reveal code or other library in the dependency graph uses it; Reveal parses JSON with Jackson.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-databind: Comparable missing from DefaultBaseTypeLimitingValidator's unsafe base types (incomplete PolymorphicTypeValidator denylist)

analysis.detail: Requires polymorphic default typing. Reveal uses default ObjectMapper settings, in which default typing is disabled, and does not use polymorphic type handling. Application code that uses Jackson directly is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-databind: InetSocketAddress deserialization triggers eager DNS resolution (SSRF)

analysis.detail: Requires deserializing JSON into java.net.InetSocketAddress. Reveal deserializes JSON only into untyped JSON trees and maps and does not enable default typing, so this type is never a deserialization target. Application code that uses Jackson directly is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-databind has a PolymorphicTypeValidator bypass via generic type parameters that allows arbitrary class instantiation

analysis.detail: Requires polymorphic typing (default typing or @JsonTypeInfo). Reveal uses default ObjectMapper settings, in which default typing is disabled, and does not use polymorphic type handling. Application code that uses Jackson directly is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-core: ReDoS: quadratic backtracking in NumberInput.PATTERN_FLOAT via looksLikeValidNumber()

analysis.detail: In jackson-databind 2.17.2 the affected method is called only when a JSON string value is converted into a numeric Java type (BigDecimal, Double, Float or Number). Reveal deserializes JSON only into untyped JSON trees and maps, which keep string values as strings, and does not call the method directly. Application code that uses Jackson directly is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-databind: Duration XMLGregorianCalendar Unbounded Number Parse DoS

analysis.detail: Requires deserializing JSON into javax.xml.datatype.Duration or XMLGregorianCalendar. Reveal deserializes JSON only into untyped JSON trees and maps and does not enable default typing, so these types are never deserialization targets. Application code that uses Jackson directly is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-core: Async parser maxNumberLength bypass via chunked digit accumulation (incomplete fix for GHSA-72hv-8253-57qq)

analysis.detail: Affects only Jackson's non-blocking (async) parser. Reveal parses JSON only with Jackson's standard blocking parser and does not use the non-blocking parser. Application code that uses Jackson directly is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-databind has an array subtype allowlist bypass in BasicPolymorphicTypeValidator (allowIfSubTypeIsArray)

analysis.detail: Requires polymorphic typing (default typing or @JsonTypeInfo). Reveal uses default ObjectMapper settings, in which default typing is disabled, and does not use polymorphic type handling. Application code that uses Jackson directly is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-databind: Incomplete fix for CVE-2026-54514: eager DNS resolution (SSRF) still present in InetAddress deserialization

analysis.detail: Requires deserializing JSON into java.net.InetAddress. Reveal deserializes JSON only into untyped JSON trees and maps and does not enable default typing, so this type is never a deserialization target. Application code that uses Jackson directly is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: Eclipse Jetty: Path parameter traversal

analysis.detail: Affects only applications that protect paths with Jetty's SecurityHandler path mappings. Reveal does not use Jetty's SecurityHandler, and jetty-security is not in the dependency graph.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-databind: Path Deserialization Missing Scheme Allowlist for FileSystemProvider Resolution

analysis.detail: Requires deserializing JSON into java.nio.file.Path. Reveal deserializes JSON only into untyped JSON trees and maps and does not enable default typing, so this type is never a deserialization target. Application code that uses Jackson directly is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: org.eclipse.jetty:jetty-http has different parsing of invalid URIs

analysis.detail: Affects applications that make security decisions based on Jetty's parsing of URI schemes, hosts or authorities. Reveal's Jetty listener and HTTP client make no such decisions; the client connects only to local engine URLs that Reveal builds itself.

vulnerabilities.description: jackson-databind retains every unknown raw type ID

analysis.detail: Applies only during polymorphic type ID resolution (@JsonTypeInfo or default typing). Reveal uses neither, so no type IDs are resolved. Application code that uses Jackson directly is outside this assessment.

vulnerabilities.description: The Eclipse Jetty Server Artifact has a Gzip request memory leak

analysis.detail: Affects only deployments that enable Jetty's GzipHandler for request decompression. Reveal does not configure GzipHandler.
